rationale: Candidate 0005 was rejected only for BF16-autocast CE output failures: its FP32 Triton CE math, once the FP32 result propagated back through BF16 rounding in the surrounding autocast region, perturbed five token-loss elements per step on steps 2/3 by max~0.00799, exceeding the unchanged atol 3e-4 / rtol 1e-3, even though every FP32 check, all CE matrices, the wide-int64 audit and the 2-layer holdout passed (FP32 complete-step geomean ~1.167). The passing model-gradient checks do not excuse the output failures, so 0005 is rejected and no tolerance/verifier/config/timer is touched. This candidate is the minimal child: the 0003 residual/RMSNorm source and the 0005 FP32 Triton CE kernels, max-shift math, process-local launch cache and exact int64 (col==target)&mask comparison are byte-identical above. The ONLY change is at the public cross_entropy entry, which now adds an active-CUDA-autocast guard using the parent's _cuda_autocast_enabled() and dispatches, when autocast is active, to a new TP=1 native-equivalent Torch autograd CE (_NativeAutocastCrossEntropy) that reproduces the pinned native VocabParallelCrossEntropy operations and their exact ordering (logits.float, torch.max, in-place subtract_ of unsqueezed max, target_mask (target<0)|(target>=V), masked_target.clone()-0 with masked_target[mask]=0, 2D view + arange advanced-index + clone().contiguous() + view_as, predicted[mask]=0.0, torch.exp out=same buffer, sum, log(sum_exp)-predicted, div_ normalize; backward view/arange, softmax_update=1-target_mask.float(), in-place grad_2d[arange,masked_target]-=softmax_update, mul_ by grad_output.unsqueeze(-1)). It does not use F.cross_entropy/log_softmax or simplified autograd, keeps loss and grad_input FP32 internally and lets autograd cast the gradient to the original logits dtype like native. Because world_size is 1, the native all_reduce(MAX) on logits_max and the two all_reduce(SUM) on predicted_logits and sum_exp_logits are the identity and are omitted; vocab_start=0, vocab_end=V. Megatron is never imported and the default world group is never touched, since the external adapter owns the TP group, the TP=1 / zero-smoothing / contiguity / dtype guards and the native fallback. Wide/out-of-range int64 labels are caught by target_mask (native log(sumexp) loss, no onehot term/subtraction); there is no ignore_index and zero smoothing only. Under autocast with BF16 input, logits.float() allocates a separate FP32 buffer so the original low-precision input is unchanged, while FP32 input preserves the native observable forward mutation; no new shape or domain claims are made. This Torch branch is a compatibility path, not Triton CE fusion under autocast, so the adapter's optimized call counter only proves the candidate API was selected, not which internal branch ran; independent audit should verify FP32 forward/backward still produce compiled GPU launches and that under active autocast the loss and gradients equal native CE with zero Triton launches. No other optimization or tuning is included, and promotion is not claimed until all 14 formal processes are rerun.
